A toothpaste company has quietly killed the entire market research industry and nobody is talking about it.

Colgate published a paper showing you can predict real purchase intent by simply asking LLMs to roleplay customers.

And this is beyond insane.

If you ask an AI, "Rate this product from 1 to 5," it gives safe, middle-of-the-road garbage.

So researchers invented a method called Semantic Similarity Rating (SSR).

Instead of asking the AI for a number, they asked it to roleplay.

They gave the LLM a demographic profile. They showed it a product concept. And they asked it to write down its raw, unfiltered thoughts.

Then, they used a semantic model to translate those written thoughts into a numerical score.

The results are staggering.

Tested against 57 real personal care product surveys and 9,300 human responses, the synthetic consumers hit 90% of human test-retest reliability.

They perfectly mirrored how different age brackets and income levels react to price changes.

Short-term holder capitulation has often come before local bottoms, but in a bear market these losses can last longer than expected.

tweet.text:
🔔 When Short-Term Holders are selling at a loss.

🔹 When the short-term holders (STH) SOPR drops below 0.993, it signals that STH are selling at a loss. It’s often when STH begin to capitulate that good opportunities may arise.

The SOPR (Spent Output Profit Ratio) is an indicator that measures the ratio of realized profit or loss generated by an STH UTXO when it is spent.

This preset alert is designed to identify good entry points on BTC for the medium to long term, especially for DCA strategies. However, it also works well for short-term trading, though it doesn’t provide exit signals.

This alert is all the more effective during bullish phases, because during bear markets the pain suffered by STH is more pronounced and lasts longer.

We currently estimate that STH are realizing an average loss of around 15%, with more and more BTC at a loss landing on exchanges. This confirms that STH are indeed realizing losses and that these aren’t just simple BTC movements.

Nick Tomaino: Lessons Learned from 15 Years in Crypto
> Run your race and focus on reality over the perception game.
> Believe in something more than money and attention.
> Lead with curiosity. Understand products; don’t just believe narratives.
> Bet on people running their own race with a belief in something more + a curious mindset.
Source:
https://x.com/NTmoney/status/2124498180289315099

tweet.text:
Lessons learned from 15 years in crypto:

1) Run your race and focus on reality over the perception game. Can’t tell you how many founders and VCs who looked “legit” here at one time have come and gone. If the timeline is shilling a narrative, it’s a good time to take the other side of the bet. The best bet is on yourself.

2) Believe in something more than money and attention. The money and attention comes and goes but long term belief in a broader mission is what will keep you engaged and growing and is the only way to win.

3) Lead with curiosity. Understand products, don’t just believe narratives. Understand what the narratives are too but be skeptical when they are projected on you too strongly. Double down on what you like.

4) Bet on people who are similarly running their own race with a belief in something more and curious mindset.

These apply outside of crypto too of course. Crypto is life.

Gm,
Market is bad. Awful.
As you know, I'm always honest here, with my wins and my mistakes.
🫡
Here is what happened with my thesis and how things got bad ↓
-------
✦
The thesis
My thesis, posted here, was that $BTC was holding $80k well, despite all the awful news:
• Clarity Act failed to pass
• Fed hiked rates
• $387M Bitget hack
• Ledger supply-chain attack
• Hotter than expected CPI
So I was bullish. This kind of bad news used to dump the whole market, it wasn't happening anymore.
I said that if we visited $80k again I'd buy, and that if we lost the level, especially below $79k, I would reassess and update here.
I didn't reassess and I didn't update.
We lost the level, and dropped sharply to $75k.
I wanted to keep my bullish bias, even if clearly the bad news was now affecting the market, and the whole market, not just crypto.
I thought it was peak fear, and that nothing worse could happen, so I bought the fear.
It was not peak fear.
I had time to cut the positions, but I didn't follow my thesis.
-------
✦
What happened
I didn't expect so much bad news back to back:
• Binance got hacked for ~$6.3B, the biggest crypto hack ever
• Part of the attack went through a compromised internal AI tool, which fed the fear around crypto hacks and AI
• Right after the US midterms, the Nasdaq 100 had its worst day since 2020 (-6.4%), with chip stocks down 12% that day
• Then the Nvidia situation, Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO after a scandal.
• Even a record quarter didn't stop the stock from falling. Dragging tech stocks & AI down
• People talking about a burst of the AI "bubble"
• Fed hike bets came back
• More war news: the US-Iran conflict escalated again, with tankers hitting mines in Hormuz
• Nasdaq 100 down 10% in a week, its worst week since March 2020, and now ~20% below its ATH
• And the whole market went down with it: stocks, crypto, even gold
-------
✦
Where I am now
Good thing is, I followed my larger plan of always keeping dry powder, as I always tell you here.
Just not enough.
I bought at $75k, and $70k (which is quite bad), but didn't try to catch the falling knife all the way down.
• I bought again around $57k, near the 2026 low from July, hoping $56k would hold
• It broke for a while, but we never went under $55k, and we got $56k back
• We also got $60k back, then lost it again, it doesn't seem to be holding easily for now
→ I'm now 70% invested in the market.
Mainly $BTC, $HYPE, $ETH, $ZEC & $SOL.
Some of it is still leveraged (3 to 5x), and I had to add margin to keep it open.
Still have 30% dry powder.
This capital should be used if we go even lower ($56k and lower), but if we have found a bottom here I'm happy with that obviously.
It also could be used for S&P500/NASDAQ100 & Gold, as the opportunity seems good right now.
(Probably 2 or 3x leverage, but I'm still watching for now).
And some stock picking, like $NVDA, which is down 48% from ATH, in less than 2 months.
I'm also eyeing some other tech stocks that are down bad, like $INTC or $TSM.
If this isn't the start of a real economic crash (I hope not), these are great opportunities.
Especially for the NVDA dump:
Best quarter ever for NVIDIA: revenue +103% in a year, and they expect even more next quarter.
Yet at ~$125, the stock costs less than 12 years of current profits. Very cheap for this growth.
The real issue is trust: Huang left after a scandal, and the SEC is reportedly looking into Nvidia's accounting.
If that comes out clean, I think the stock should bounce back fast.
And so will other AI & tech stocks.
Just a cool off. Not the burst of the "AI Bubble".
Could be generational prices, we'll see.
